Project overview presentation based on the implemented local Docker prototype.
College systems need both high public availability and strong protection for sensitive records.
Admission deadlines and result publication create sudden spikes in student traffic.
Academic marks and financial transactions require restricted access.
One system must connect both workloads without exposing the private database.
Build a working college portal that separates public and private workloads, authenticates users with JWT, and demonstrates load balancing with cloud bursting.
Focus: a clear architecture that can be demonstrated during project evaluation.

No external deployment claim: the project models the architecture locally using Docker networks.

Implemented modules mirror the public-cloud and private-cloud workload separation described in the project abstract.
Nginx exposes only the public entry point. Private services and data remain on internal networks.
The browser never receives a direct route to the private API or private database.

Architecture reflects the Compose topology: proxy on public network, public API bridging the internal hybrid network, and private DB on a separate internal network.
Each component sits in the environment that matches its traffic profile and sensitivity.

The public API accesses private data only through the simulated hybrid-cloud connection.
JWT validates the student at the public edge. A separate short-lived token protects the internal private request.
Student sends credentials to the public API
Public API returns a JWT with user ID and role
Public API validates JWT and creates a 60-second internal token
Private API verifies service purpose and record ownership
Academic or finance records return through the gateway
Student ownership rule: students can request only their own private records.
